title: Operator session
source: An operator interface on its own WebSocket: hello, the pushed picture, a repeating query, a command accepted, one refused, and a cancel.

steps.why: The operator interface opens its WebSocket and says hello with its operator_id and key, the only message that carries the key.
Core checks the key against its stored hash and accepts.
Core pushes each Asset's stored admin.describe unchanged (A1 here). Same from, seq and time as the Asset sent.
And A2, a receive-only ADS-B receiver that accepts no commands.
Core pushes A1's latest state: settings,
health,
and position. From here on Core forwards new reports as they arrive; nothing is polled.
The operator asks for A1's battery every 30 s.
Core sends A1's latest battery report unchanged, including its from, seq and time. Each 30 s repeat reaches readers with the original measurement time.
Then Core accepts the query. A query's reply comes after its answer, so it marks the end.
The operator adds a takeoff Task, T4, for A1: its body first.
A1 lists takeoff in its describe, so Core accepts and passes the body to A1 unchanged.
Then A1's new task list, built on the version it last saw. Core checks it and passes it on unchanged (its admin.reply is not shown).
A1 holds T4's body, so the list takes effect; its queue report names the list it answers.
A mistaken takeoff for A2.
A2 lists no commands, so Core refuses with a reason and sends nothing to A2.
The operator removes T4 by sending A1 an empty list.
Core accepts and passes the list on to A1.
T4 left the list without starting, so A1 reports it cancelled.
A failsafe is forwarded the moment it arrives.
The operator asks for A1's path over the first 100 s.
Core sends each stored telemetry report, oldest first (one here).
The reply marks the end of the answer. Had nothing matched, this reply would come alone.
